 THE TIMES OF INDIA | Oct 27, 2026, 13:49:11 IST SUMMARY India vs New Zealand Live Score, 3rd T20: India will have the chance to put their recent T20I troubles behind them and seal the series against New Zealand when the two sides meet in the third match at Hnry Stadium in Wellington on Tuesday. Shreyas Iyer’s team have won the opening two games and will be keen to carry that momentum into a contest where strong winds and potentially tricky weather could test their adaptability. 
 The Men in Blue have endured a mixed run since lifting the T20 World Cup. Defeats in Ireland, a disappointing 4-0 series loss in England and a 2-2 draw against the West Indies at home highlighted their inability to finish matches consistently. The recent victories in New Zealand, however, have provided encouraging signs of progress. 
 India began the tour with a successful chase of 225 before producing a resilient performance in the second T20I. After slipping to 70/5, they recovered to chase down New Zealand’s 180, with Naman Dhir, Tilak Varma and Nitish Kumar Reddy holding their nerve under pressure. 
 Teenager Vaibhav Sooryavanshi is expected to feature again at No.3, with Ishan Kishan unavailable for the third match. The youngster will be eager to make the most of the opportunity as India look to maintain their aggressive approach. 
 Bowling coach Morne Morkel has emphasised the need to raise standards and avoid excuses after the team’s earlier inconsistencies. Wellington’s swirling winds could make conditions challenging, although the forecast suggests the rain should clear before the scheduled 8 PM local start. 
 New Zealand will be without Matt Henry for the remainder of the series, while Lockie Ferguson is also set to miss the match. Despite those absences, the hosts will look to respond after losing the first two games. India have won 18 of their 21 T20Is against New Zealand this decade and will aim to add another victory to that impressive record while securing the series. Commentary

Pitched fuller and quicker, on the off stump. Phillips takes a step forward and tries to bludgeon it over the bowler's head, but fails to get under it properly. Ends up hitting it off the inner half and offers a simple return catch to Axar. He drags both hands to his left and plucks it around his chest. New Zealand are 123/3, with the dangerous Phillips gone.

However, with Mitchell well set now and Phillips, featuring in his 100th T20I, the platform is very much set for these two to keep hammering runs. Conditions look pretty good for batting so it looks like another 200-plus total is on the cards.

The opening two matches in New Zealand have offered encouragement. India chased down 225 in the first T20I before recovering from 70/5 to secure a four-wicket victory in the second. With Ishan Kishan ruled out of the third match, teenager Vaibhav Sooryavanshi is expected to get another opportunity at No.3. India will also need to adjust to Wellington’s challenging weather, with strong winds and the possibility of rain adding another layer of difficulty.
Bowling coach Morne Morkel has stressed the importance of maintaining an aggressive approach and eliminating excuses. New Zealand, meanwhile, will aim to stay competitive despite the absence of Matt Henry and Lockie Ferguson.
